messages:
Alice M: FYI, we just saw a control-plane spike in eu-west-1 tied to a Kafka broker flapping. Im initiating a deploy freeze for any releases that touch routing/controlplane in EU. Please dont push new canaries there.

deploy-bot: deploys: PAUSED for tags matching: region:eu OR service:controlplane OR service:router. Affected queues: canary, staged-rollout. Reason: incident-171820. To override, react :no_entry: and ping #eng-releases.

Ben (platform): @Alice M thanks. Can non-EU deploys continue? we have a couple of infra tweaks queued that are global but not touching controlplane.

Alice M: Non-EU can continue if they do NOT touch kafka/controlplane routing or rollout orchestration. If it references shared infra (schema migrations, cert rotations) hold until ops confirms.

ops-oncall: short update: broker is flapping due to a rolling maintenance that overlapped a config change. Team is rolling back the config and bringing brokers back. ETA ~20-30m for stabilization. No data loss observed.

Carol: Should we pin the current service versions for the queued releases so the deploy system won't auto-promote? I'm getting asked by a couple of PMs.

Alice M: Yes, please pin the rollouts for affected services. Use the console: set rollout.lock = true on the release in question or tag the commit with "hold/incident-171820".

Dana: Quick checklist I'm applying:
- pin versions for services: controlplane, routing, auth
- cancel canaries for EU zones
- re-run smoke tests in staging after ops confirms
- prepare rollback artifacts for last known-good
I'll post exact commands in a sec.

Ben (platform): For the commits already in pipeline, do we want to do a soft-rollback (fast fallback) or just prevent promotion and let them queue? Some teams prefer immediate rollback.

Alice M: Don't rollback globally yet. Prevent promotion and pin. If ops says brokers unstable after stabilization, we'll do targeted rollback per-service. We want to avoid cascading changes.

Dana: commands: 
```
# pin current deploy
redwoodctl rollout pin --service controlplane --reason "incident-171820"
redwoodctl rollout cancel --zone eu-west-1 --tag canary
```

deploy-bot: Action taken: pinned rollouts for services: controlplane, router, auth. Cancelled canary queues in eu-west-1. Job ids: 38922,38923.

ops-oncall: brokers are back to steady for last 5m. We're monitoring. If you want a controlled resume, suggest a 2-step: canary small %, then 10m watch, then larger.

Carol: Thanks — I'll update the release notes and tell PMs we paused promotion and pinned versions. Also will schedule a gated canary re-run for only non-kafka touch changes.

Ben (platform): When we resume, can we use the lighter kernel for controlplane (the kvcache tweak) or is that blocked? Need to know for deploy window.

Alice M: Kernel/optimization changes that touch runtime are blocked until we verify stability. Minor client-side flags ok.

Dana: I'll prepare the post-incident checklist for resuming: smoke + perf checks, 5m small canary, 15m medium canary, manual approval to full.

Alice M: Great. I'll keep this thread as the coordination channel. If ops gives the all-clear, I'll unpin and schedule a staggered resume with ops and platform oncall. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reschedule note: blocked deploys will be re-evaluated in 45m. To schedule a manual resume: `redwoodctl rollout resume --window "staggered" --approver @Alice M`

Carol: Copy. Posting update to release notes and PMs now.

ops-oncall: will post final after 30m if stable.

Alice M: thanks everyone. keep changes minimal until we get green.
